land.text: Greece as Cliopatria's last pre-war shape (1940), before the Axis occupation of 1941-44, which no Cliopatria row covers

predecessors.note: The page: 'The monarchy was restored in 1935, after a referendum'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Greece row starts only in 1945, after the German withdrawal and the return of the government in exile to Athens.

land.text: the Greek state under the colonels, from the coup of 21 April 1967

successors.note: The monarchy itself lasted formally to 1 June 1973, when 'the Greek military junta unilaterally abolished the monarchy'; Cliopatria's Kingdom row ends in 1966 and its junta row starts in 1967, and this dossier follows that split.

correction.text: mainland Greece and the Aegean and Ionian islands without the Dodecanese: after 8 May 1945 'the islands became a British military protectorate' and were united with Greece only in 1947

keyframe_review.note: 122,017 km2 for 1945. The shape contains 6 of the 9 Dodecanese grid cells, though the German garrison surrendered the islands to the British on Rhodes on 8 May 1945 and Italy gave them up only in the 1947 peace treaty. The Kingdom page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is not possible; the only figure on the pages is the Dodecanese at 2,714 km2 (the Dodecanese page).

correction.text: the whole kingdom without the Dodecanese; the Democratic Army's northern mountains are contested land (ledger, from March 1946), not land removed

keyframe_review.note: 99,568 km2: Cliopatria cuts 78 cells (73 of them in Greece proper: Western and Central Macedonia, Epirus, Thessaly, Sterea Ellada, Thrace) out of the 1945 shape for 1946. The page dates the resumed fighting to March 1946 ('Fighting resumed in March 1946 after an attack on a police station at Litochoro') and the Democratic Army to December 1946, and describes its operations as attacks after which 'the DSE melted back into the mountains'; it gives no frontier of rebel-held land in 1946, so the removal is not supported and is drawn as contested land instead.

correction.text: the whole kingdom including the Dodecanese, handed over by Italy in 1947; the north is contested land, not removed

keyframe_review.note: 105,345 km2. Same reasoning as 1946: the page speaks of 1947 'large-scale attacks on towns across northern Epirus, Thessaly, Peloponnese, and Macedonia' and the formation of a Provisional Democratic Government on 23-24 December 1947, which 'no foreign government recognized'; no held territory is stated. The Dodecanese join Greece in 1947 and are in the 1949 shape.

correction.text: the whole kingdom; the northern mountains and, for the year, the Peloponnese are contested land

keyframe_review.note: 116,274 km2. The one page statement of rebel control is the III Division 'controlled 70% of the Peloponnese politically and militarily' in 1948 before its 'huge defeat' in summer 1948, which the ledger records as a contest on the Peloponnese for 1948; the Cliopatria shape does not remove the Peloponnese (82 of 101 cells present).

122,017 km2 for 1949-62, the same cells as 1945: the whole kingdom. The Kingdom page: 'The postwar settlement saw Greece's territorial expansion, which had begun in 1832, come to an end', and the Dodecanese were the only addition. The Democratic Army's last divisions retreated to Albania in September 1949. The shape stands (it contains the Dodecanese from 1949).

122,017 km2 for 1963-66, cell for cell the shape of 1949-62 (Cliopatria splits the row at 1963 with no change). Nothing on the pages moves the frontier before the coup of 21 April 1967; the Kingdom ends in this dossier in April 1967 and the junta row starts in 1967.

region.text: Greece as Cliopatria's last pre-war shape (1940), which the Kingdom of Greece keeps until the German conquest of April 1941

ledger.note: 1941: the Kingdom of Greece is drawn from 1 January 1941, the year after Cliopatria's First Hellenic Republic row ends (1940), so that the Greek state does not vanish from the map. The page: the monarchy 'was restored in 1935, after a referendum'; Italian troops 'crossed the border on 28 October 1940' and Germany 'attacked Greece through Yugoslavia and Bulgaria on 6 April 1941'; after the fall of Greece 'The king and the government escaped to Crete' and then to Egypt, 'where a government in exile was established'; 'German forces withdrew on 12 October 1944' and 'the government in exile returned to Athens'. The Hellenic State (hellenic-state/ledger/0, April 1941) takes the mainland from this dossier, and its ledger/10 hands the land back in October 1944. Fix fx-50 (3 Nov 2026, R143): before this event the dossier began in 1945, so first-hellenic-republic's end-1940 successor entry had no living dossier to take the land (390 cells to nobody from 1 January to April 1941) and the Hellenic State's October 1944 loss to this dossier went to nobody until 1945.

region.text: Greece after the German withdrawal, without the Dodecanese

ledger.note: 1945: the restored Kingdom of Greece governs from Athens. The page: 'The monarchy was restored in 1935, after a referendum', and after the German withdrawal 'the government in exile returned to Athens'; the 1945 start is Cliopatria's row, the page gives no 1944-45 date. Fix fx-50: this was the found event of 1945; the dossier now starts in January 1941 (the previous event), and this one takes whatever of the 1945 shape nobody holds.

region.text: the mountains of northern Greece, 'the two key positions in northern Greece for the DSE' being Grammos and Vitsi; fighting resumed at Litochoro

ledger.note: March 1946: the civil war resumes in northern Greece. 'Fighting resumed in March 1946 after an attack on a police station at Litochoro' (infobox start 31 March 1946); the Democratic Army appears from December 1946 and in 1947 'launched large-scale attacks on towns across northern Epirus, Thessaly, Peloponnese, and Macedonia'. The page gives no boundary of the contested land; the four northern regions are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Dodecanese: 'formally united with Greece by the 1947 Peace Treaty with Italy'

ledger.note: 1947: the Dodecanese join Greece. 'The islands joined Greece in 1947 following as the Governorate-General of the Dodecanese'; Italy had held them since 1912, and after 8 May 1945 they were a British military protectorate. The Paris treaty was signed on 10 February 1947 and entered into force on 15 September 1947 (Paris Peace Treaties page: 'The Dodecanese Islands were ceded to Greece'). The day of the handover and the 1948 formal union are not on the pages opened.

region.text: the Peloponnese, where III Division 'controlled 70% of the Peloponnese politically and militarily'

ledger.note: 1948: the Democratic Army holds most of the Peloponnese. 'III Division, with 20,000 men in 1948, controlled 70% of the Peloponnese politically and militarily'; the page gives no month for the start and a different strength (1,000 to 5,000 fighters) for early 1948.

region.text: the Peloponnese, 'In summer 1948, DSE Division III in the Peloponnese suffered a huge defeat'

ledger.note: Summer 1948: the National Army's plan 'Peristera' clears the Peloponnese; the page gives no day.

region.text: northern Greece, where the main DSE divisions at Grammos and Vitsi 'retreated to Albania' in September 1949

ledger.note: 1949: the civil war ends. The infobox gives 30 August 1949; Papagos's 'Operation Pyrsos' (Torch) opened in August; Tito closed the Yugoslav border in July 1949; Zachariadis announced a ceasefire on 16 October 1949, which the text calls the end of the war.

region.text: Greece, as the kingdom held it to the coup

ledger.note: 21 April 1967: the colonels seize power. 'On 21 April 1967 however, a group of right-wing colonels ... seized power'; the monarchy was abolished only on 1 June 1973.

wars.name: Greek Civil War

zones.text: northern Greece: Grammos, Vitsi and the Epirus, Macedonia and Thessaly mountains

wars.outcome: Government victory: the Democratic Army's main divisions retreated to Albania in September 1949 after Operation Pyrsos; infobox end 30 August 1949, ceasefire announced 16 October 1949.
wars.note: The page gives no stable rebel-held territory except the 1948 Peloponnese claim, so no rebel-state dossier is written. Britain, which had 'spent 85 million pounds in Greece since 1944', could not go on, and the Truman Doctrine (1947) brought US support. The earlier Dekemvriana (3 December 1944, 37 days in Athens) falls before this state's row.

certainty.note: The state's land in the occupation years is the pre-war shape minus what the Hellenic State dossier takes; only a few islands stay in this dossier (about 13 cells), the rest of the map is the occupation zones.
Greece's frontiers are treaty lines; the Dodecanese line is the 1947 treaty's; the contested northern mountains 1946-49 are soft, being fought land with no drawn boundary.

notes:
Cliopatria row: Kingdom of Greece 1945..1966, six shapes; its successor greek-junta 1967..1975 and third-hellenic-republic 1976.. are other eu-22 parts' rows, and the predecessor row is first-hellenic-republic (1822..1940). Four of six verdicts are 'adjust': 1945-46 contain 6 Dodecanese cells before the 1947 transfer; 1946-48 remove 72, 53 and 18 further cells of northern and central Greece for a rebel zone that the page does not map. The year-by-year extent of the Democratic Army's control is NOT on the Wikipedia pages opened (the page says 'Not on the page' for Pindus, Olympus, Evros, Taygetus and Roumeli); only the 1948 Peloponnese claim and the Grammos and Vitsi strongholds are named, so the contest events are coarse and a gap-filler with a detailed map source (the Battle of Grammos-Vitsi article, which was not opened) could narrow them. No rebel dossier: the page says the Provisional Democratic Government (23-24 December 1947) was unrecognised and describes DSE operations as attacks followed by retreat.

Not settled within the page budget: the exact day of the Dodecanese handover (31 March 1947 and the union of 7 March 1948 are not on the pages opened); the Greek claim on Northern Epirus (a claim only: 'Greek nationalists continued to claim southern Albania', no frontier change); the Greek rulers (George II, Paul, Constantine II dates are not on the Kingdom page, so identity.rulers is omitted); Greek-Albanian relations (people-s-socialist-republic-of-albania, neighbour 1946-1966). Western Thrace and Eastern Macedonia are returned by the Paris treaty page's wording ('Regained Eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace from Bulgaria'), already inside the 1945 shape.

No gazetteer names needed: {region: Dodecanese} and the four admin-1 names resolve.
